name: frontend
//resolutions: Audited 2026-08-20 against the npm advisory API, version by version: every pin below was checked to be at or above the fixed version of the advisory it exists for. Two had gone stale and were bumped - form-data 4.0.4 -> 4.0.6 (GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx, CRLF injection, fixed in 4.0.6) and js-yaml 4.1.1 -> 4.3.1 (GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m and GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj, quadratic-complexity DoS, fixed in 4.3.1). Both were pinned when those versions WERE the fix; upstream then moved the floor, axios and @eslint/eslintrc asked for the newer range, and the pins were what held the vulnerable copy in place - yarn says so on every install, one 'Resolution field ... is incompatible with requested version' line per stale pin. Treat that warning as the signal to re-run this check. A pin can also warn for the opposite, legitimate reason - being an UPGRADE past what the parent asks for. @eslint/plugin-kit was pinned to 0.3.4 for exactly that, because eslint 9.23.0 asked for ^0.2.7 and GHSA-xffm-g5w8-qvg7 affects <0.3.4. It was dropped on 2026-08-20 by fixing the cause instead: eslint 9.39.5 asks for ^0.4.1, which is past the advisory on its own, and holding 0.3.4 against it would have turned that pin into a downgrade within one release - the same failure the two above had already walked into. Upgrade the parent where you can; pin only where you cannot. Pins left over from react-scripts/craco/webpack matched nothing and were removed on 2026-08-18. The rollup pin went the same way on 2026-08-20, for a different reason: react-qr-reader was the only thing that pulled rollup in, and react-qr-reader itself was removed as unused, so the pin now matches nothing. The entries that remain are live CVE mitigations - do not drop one without re-running the check. See frontend/README.md for the method.
